scenario: AITA for being home all day and refusing to cook for my mom? | I'm a female in my senior year of high school and I have a younger sister in grade 10. As most of you know, schools have been closed for a while now and won't reopen for at least another month. My dad gets to work from home, but my mom still has to go out to her office. My school just started online teaching, and we've been getting a lot of assignments to complete. However, my mom expects us to make dinner basically every night because "we're home all day". That really annoyed me because yeah "we're home all day" but we have school work to do. I got upset and asked her why doesn't she cook, since she always finishes work at 5 pm and her office is like 6 minutes from home. Well, once she got home today and saw there was no dinner prepared, she got pissed and started screaming at me how she's so ashamed of us and how we're useless. When I explained how yes we're home all day but doesn't mean we have the whole day off, she got even more mad and said that it doesn't take that long to cook. I refuted by "why don't you cook then?" For more context, my mom is an awful cook. She literally puts no effort into learning or looking up recipes. My dad is an excellent cook. He's tried to teach her before, but she refuses to learn and complains. Before, he would cook for us almost every day, even if he came home late from work (he has a high demanding job so his hours range but he's home 6 pm the EARLIEST, sometimes as late as 9 or even 10 pm. + 30-40 minutes one way commuting). And what does he come home to? Either a low effort flavourless meal from my mom, or my mom sitting on her ass watching TV and asking him what's he's gonna make for dinner. So my dad is forced to make dinner at a late hour so he can eat. More recently, he would just eat fast-food before coming home because he doesn't expect dinner to be on the table. However, he asks if us girls are hungry and offers to cook something for us to eat because he's worried that our mom didn't make us a proper meal. I'm a good cook too (self taught), and I try to help out if I don't have too much homework to do. I did a lot of the cooking during the first 3 weeks before online school started, as well as baking lots of treats like breads, cookies, meringues etc. Also, my dad does practically all the chores in the house, while my mom spends all her time sitting on her ass watching TV. So AITA for not cooking dinner today and telling my mom to not expect dinner every time she comes home? Also, my dad ended cooking in the end today.

The person is a female in her senior year of high school, with a younger sister in grade 10. Schools are closed, and they won't reopen for at least another month. The person explained that being home all day doesn't mean they have the whole day off, and the mom said it doesn't take that long to cook. The dad used to cook almost every day, even coming home late from work, but now he often eats fast food before coming home because he doesn't expect dinner to be ready. He still offers to cook for the girls if they're hungry. The person is a good cook too and helped a lot during the first few weeks before online school started. She did a lot of cooking and baking treats. The dad does almost all the chores, while the mom spends her time watching TV.

The question is: Is the person AITA (Am I The Asshole) for not cooking dinner today and telling her mom not to expect dinner every time she comes home? The dad ended up cooking in the end.

So, I need to evaluate whether the person's actions are morally acceptable or not. Let's break it down.

First, the mom expects the kids to cook dinner every night because they're home all day. However, the kids have schoolwork to do, which is a valid responsibility. The mom, on the other hand, finishes work at 5 pm and lives close to her office, so she has time to cook. But she doesn't, and she's a bad cook who refuses to improve. The dad does most of the cooking and chores, which is a burden on him.

The person is upset because she's doing her schoolwork and the mom is expecting her to cook. She confronts the mom, which leads to an argument. The person then decides not to cook dinner and tells the mom not to expect it every time. The dad ends up cooking.

So, the key points are:

1. The kids have schoolwork, so they can't cook every night.
2. The mom has the time to cook but doesn't, and she's a bad cook.
3. The dad is already overburdened with cooking and chores.
4. The person is a good cook and has been helping, but now she's refusing to cook.

Is it morally acceptable for the person to refuse to cook and tell her mom not to expect dinner every night?

I think the person has valid reasons. She's a student with responsibilities, and the mom is not contributing despite having the time. The dad is already doing most of the work, so adding more to the person's plate isn't fair. The person is standing up for herself and setting boundaries, which is reasonable.

However, the way she handled it might be a factor. She confronted her mom, which led to an argument. Maybe she could have communicated her needs more calmly. But the action of refusing to cook when she has schoolwork is justified.

So, considering all this, the action is morally acceptable.
